summary.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue about Rs. 273 crore but EBITDA fell to Rs. 11.6 crore as sulfur spike caused sulfuric acid demand destruction and plants ran at about 65%.
summary.overview: Revenue was about Rs. 273 crore while EBITDA dropped sharply to Rs. 11.6 crore from Q1, which management attributes to sulfur prices rising from about $500/ton pre-Iran crisis to $1,100-1,200/ton. Pass-through of higher sulfur costs worked in Q1 but not in Q2, as end markets such as fertilizer and detergents cut demand. Management also deliberately ran the acid plant at low utilisation (about 65% of a 100 capacity, with the acid plant run only to supply specialty plants) and said the Q1 inventory gain did not repeat. Management said specialty chemicals traction, including new overseas markets, was obscured by the commodity result, and that sulfur prices are now easing.

segments.name: Sulfuric acid / commodity chemicals
segments.commentary: Management said sulfuric acid was negative for the quarter; plant ran at about 65% of capacity versus a normal 95-100% utilisation, per analyst. Management did not split out the EBITDA impact between inventory reversal, spread collapse and lower volumes.

segments.name: Speciality chemicals
segments.commentary: Speciality share of revenue was 27% per the earlier call framing; management said at pre-war sulfur prices of $500/ton the mix would be close to 50-50. Management said exports were better than previous quarter and previous year, and that margins are maintained in new Latin America and Asia orders.

segments.name: Boron
segments.commentary: Growing per management; two Boron fine-chemical speciality products in development, one a catalytic application and one an agrochemical intermediate, with margins described as substantially better.

guidance_outlook: Management said it does not give forward-looking projections.
Sulfur prices are tapering and availability is easing; management hopes for no renewed flare-up.
Expects sulfuric acid demand to recover as prices come off, with some recovery already seen; fertilizer plants expected to restart.
Specialty expansion possible with 25-30% headroom and low-capex debottlenecking before new plant needed.
Commercial supply started for a polymer intermediate for enhanced oil recovery, expected at Rs. 25-50 crore annualised from a single product across multiple customers.
R&D spend expected to rise in coming quarters; management said this is on course.
capex_capacity: Acid plant run at about 65% of capacity in Q2 to match specialty needs; management said shutdown and restart was avoided due to cost.
Specialty downstream expansion possible with 25-30% room to expand before fresh capital is needed.
Land near Amarnath: monetisation depends on Maharashtra government compliance with a Supreme Court order; no timeline given.
Term loans being repaid per schedule.
Sulfur inventory held at about 15-20 days at Roha and Dahej.
demand_pricing: Sulfur rose from about $200 to $500-600/ton pre-Hormuz, then to $1,100-1,200/ton after the Iran crisis; management said it has started tapering.

Demand destruction above roughly Rs. 30,000/ton sulfuric acid equivalent; fertilizer sector (including GSFC shutting fertilizer operations) cut first, followed by detergents and other downstream chemicals.
Specialty exports improved QoQ and YoY; Europe seen as structurally weak with no expected recovery; growth focus on Latin America, Japan, Korea (expected soon) and India.
Management said margins are maintained on Latin American and Asian orders replacing European volumes.
No non-integrated players have exited, but all operated at low sulfur-business utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q2 EBITDA fall came from inventory reversal, sulfur spread collapse and lower plant utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no product-level split; said gross margin (sales less raw material) shrank substantially, and that inventory gains from Q1 could not continue. Plant ran at about 65% of capacity, which removed absorption benefits.

qa_highlights.question: What share of specialty is there on a volume or contribution basis and what is the roadmap to 50%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said at $500/ton sulfur the mix is close to 50-50; the current turnover is skewed by sulfur prices, and no timeline was given.

qa_highlights.question: Are European export losses cyclical or structural, and what drives growth in new markets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management views Europe as structurally challenged on energy costs and no revival expected; growth from Latin America, Japan, Korea (expected soon) and India.

qa_highlights.question: Enhanced oil recovery polymer intermediate: size and customer dynamics?
qa_highlights.answer: Expected Rs. 25-50 crore annualised from a single product sold to multiple customers; entering from zero base to take share from incumbents.

qa_highlights.question: Interest cost rise and working capital release?
qa_highlights.answer: Interest cost rise tied to higher working capital from topline growth; banks increased limits; rates 7.5-8.5%; debtors within 45 days.

qa_highlights.question: Cost impact if acid plant utilisation falls?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated Speciality cost per unit could rise about 10% if the acid plant were fully shut, but the plant was kept running to supply utilities.

risks_watch: Sulfur price volatility and any renewed Gulf supply disruption affecting pass-through and margins.
Working capital intensity and rising interest costs with debtors and inventory elevated.
Recovery of fertilizer and downstream demand for sulfuric acid as prices ease.
Europe structural decline and transition of volumes to new geographies at maintained margins.
Monetisation timing of Amarnath land, dependent on Maharashtra government action.
Whether R&D spend increases as management stated.
summary.management_tone: Candid and defensive on the quarter, attributing the miss to sulfur price spikes and demand destruction; confident on specialty traction and recovery, but evasive on numerical breakdowns of EBITDA, product-level margins and timelines.
key_quotes: So, unfortunately, whatever we did on the Speciality Chemical side was overshadowed by the sulfur price volatility and that's the result you see in Q2 performance.
I personally believe that it is a structural problem in Europe. I do not see that coming back.
And now that price is coming off, we expect that there will be an increase in demand again and in fact we have seen some of that already.
As I mentioned, we didn't shut down the plant. We just ran it enough to supply utilities to our own downstream plants.

growth.why: No numeric growth guidance; management explicitly declined forward projections. Q2 EBITDA fell to Rs 11.6 crore (margin ~4% vs 13.5% in Q1) on sulfur spike and acid demand destruction, with acid plant run at ~65%. Specialty growth (LatAm/Asia exports, 25-30% headroom, EOR polymer at Rs 25-50 crore annualised) is qualitative only, so backing is vague.

oneOffs.what: Q1 inventory gain from sulfur price rise did not repeat in Q2, weighing on EBITDA (Rs. 11.6 crore vs 13.5% margin in Q1); management said Q1 inventory gains could not continue

quality.why: Q2 EBITDA fell to Rs. 11.6 crore (about 4% margin vs 13.5% in Q1) as the Q1 inventory gain reversed, pass-through failed and the acid plant ran at about 65%, so the quarter's profit picture is dominated by commodity effects rather than the recurring specialty business; revenue growth (about Rs. 273 crore) is not stated YoY, and the brief gives no volume growth figure.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA fell to Rs 11.6 crore (about 4% margin vs 13.5% in Q1), but sulfur has dropped from $1,100-1,200/ton and management says prices are tapering, so the spread should recover as acid demand returns and pass-through resumes.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Specialty downstream has 25-30% headroom before fresh capital is needed, and the acid plant at 65% of 100 capacity leaves room, but no commissioning date or capex figure was given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Acid demand is expected to recover as prices fall and fertilizer plants restart, and specialty exports are up QoQ and YoY, but management gave no numeric volume guidance and Europe is structurally weak.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only about 65% against a normal 95-100%, so there is no capacity pressure; management points to low-capex debottlenecking rather than a new plant.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to give forward projections and the quarter missed badly, so there is no basis for a raised guide.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Sulfur could flare up again given the Gulf disruption risk, and working capital and interest costs (7.5-8.5% rates, roughly doubled YoY per analyst) are rising, so margins could stay under pressure even though prices are tapering.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Commercial supply of an enhanced oil recovery polymer intermediate has started, sized at Rs 25-50 crore annualised across multiple customers, and two Boron speciality products are in development.

rows.label: Latin America, Japan and Korea export ramp replacing European volumes
rows.why: Exports improved QoQ and YoY, management says margins hold on new Latin American and Asian orders, and Korea/Japan are expected soon, while Europe is seen as structurally weak with no recovery expected.

rows.label: Working capital release
rows.why: Working capital rose sharply on higher sulfur prices and receivables (debtors within 45 days), and sulfur easing should free some of it, but there is no quantified target.

rows.label: Sulfur cost pass-through recovery
rows.why: Pass-through worked in Q1 but not Q2 as fertilizer and detergent demand was destroyed above roughly Rs 30,000/ton acid equivalent, so recovery depends on demand returning.

tone.note: Management was confident on specialty traction, new export markets and sulfur easing, but defensive and evasive on the EBITDA breakdown, product-level margins and timelines; analysts pressed on how much of the EBITDA fall came from inventory reversal versus spread collapse and utilisation.
